task_message:
Case F28: segment the fibrous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 211x211x355 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
I've finished the case. Summary of the work:

- **Exploration**: Scanned the volume in axial, coronal and sagittal planes with contact sheets, then inspected individual slices at full resolution to map the anatomy and the skin markers over the palpable abnormality.
- **Findings**: A large, homogeneous, T2-hypointense intramuscular mass with a well-defined capsule/fat plane in the limb, consistent with a fibrous soft-tissue tumor. The main competing structures (large bright-rimmed oval = displaced normal structure/vessel, subcutaneous fat, and the superficial fat/septal tissue under the markers) were tested with prompts and judged not to be the lesion (small sliver / fat only).
- **Segmentation**: Seeded the model at the center of the dark mass on axial slice 291, refined by checking the three orthogonal planes, and rejected the intensity-based candidate expansions (C1–C4, which mainly added subcutaneous fat and normal muscle). An over-inclusive prompt was undone back to the clean v1 result.
- **Final**: Mask v1, 338 mL, one dominant component, extent axial 196–354 (the mass reaches the superior volume edge), coronal 59–145, sagittal 64–132 — saved with medium confidence.
